## One-Sentence Summary

A mobile app that aggregates local yard, estate, and community sales on a single live map, plans efficient routes, and adds game-like rewards to turn bargain hunting into a community-strengthening adventure.

## Problem

The creators describe weekend "treasure hunts" devolving into frustrating scavenger work: listings are scattered across social groups, random sites, fading street signs, and half-remembered addresses, causing wasted time, fuel, and missed finds. There's no comprehensive, real-time map for all types of sales, making planning difficult and inefficient.

## Solution / Product Overview

The product centralizes every kind of local sale---yard, estate, flea, vendor markets, church bazaars, and pop-ups---onto one interactive map. It helps users discover events any day of the week, plot an organized route, and enjoy a "modern treasure hunt" that also channels foot traffic to nearby small businesses.

## Key Features & Capabilities

-   Unified discovery of multiple sale types (yard, estate, flea, vendor fairs, church bazaars, neighborhood pop-ups).

-   Route planning to streamline multi-stop outings.

-   Gamification: surprise "Treasure Drops," collectible "doubloons," community leaderboards, and an in-app redemption area ("Plunder Pantry") for real-world merchandise.

-   Local-business support: optional geo-fenced ads that surface modest, location-triggered offers from nearby shops.

-   Emphasis on reuse/upcycling by keeping quality goods in circulation and out of landfills.

## Target Users & Use Cases

Designed for families, casual shoppers, and serious resellers seeking efficient discovery of local sales; for community explorers who want an engaging weekend activity; and for nearby small businesses aiming to reach shoppers traveling between sale stops.

## Why Crowdfunding / Use of Funds

Support is framed as enabling development of a single-map hub that helps shoppers, sellers, and local businesses thrive together; energizes neighborhood commerce; and advances reuse. The team also cites efforts to build an audience via community connections and targeted marketing.

## Risks & Challenges

-   **App development & dependencies:** Feature additions, testing needs, or changes by third-party mapping/payment services could cause delays. Mitigation: use an experienced development team, set clear milestones, and provide regular updates.

-   **Physical reward fulfillment:** Merchandise depends on printing/production/shipping schedules. Mitigation: reliable suppliers already sourced; timelines to be confirmed before fulfillment; prompt communication and timeline adjustments if needed.

-   **Audience growth:** Adoption depends on attracting both shoppers and sellers. Mitigation: active social outreach, local-business partnerships, and planned marketing campaigns. The creators commit to transparent communication, regular progress reports, and keeping supporters informed throughout.

## Team & Partnerships

The project is led by the founders, drawing on an experienced development team for build/testing. The page mentions relationships with reliable merchandise suppliers and outreach to local businesses; no specific organizations or individuals are named.

## Support & Post-Launch Plans

The team promises regular updates and open communication about progress and any changes to delivery expectations.

## One-Sentence Summary

A mobile app that aggregates local yard, estate, and community sales on a single live map, plans efficient routes, and adds game-like rewards to turn bargain hunting into a community-strengthening adventure.

## Problem

The creators describe weekend "treasure hunts" devolving into frustrating scavenger work: listings are scattered across social groups, random sites, fading street signs, and half-remembered addresses, causing wasted time, fuel, and missed finds. There's no comprehensive, real-time map for all types of sales, making planning difficult and inefficient.

## Solution / Product Overview

The product centralizes every kind of local sale---yard, estate, flea, vendor markets, church bazaars, and pop-ups---onto one interactive map. It helps users discover events any day of the week, plot an organized route, and enjoy a "modern treasure hunt" that also channels foot traffic to nearby small businesses.

## Key Features & Capabilities

-   Unified discovery of multiple sale types (yard, estate, flea, vendor fairs, church bazaars, neighborhood pop-ups).
-   Route planning to streamline multi-stop outings.
-   Gamification: surprise "Treasure Drops," collectible "doubloons," community leaderboards, and an in-app redemption area ("Plunder Pantry") for real-world merchandise.
-   Local-business support: optional geo-fenced ads that surface modest, location-triggered offers from nearby shops.
-   Emphasis on reuse/upcycling by keeping quality goods in circulation and out of landfills.

## Target Users & Use Cases

Designed for families, casual shoppers, and serious resellers seeking efficient discovery of local sales; for community explorers who want an engaging weekend activity; and for nearby small businesses aiming to reach shoppers traveling between sale stops.

## Why Crowdfunding / Use of Funds

Support is framed as enabling development of a single-map hub that helps shoppers, sellers, and local businesses thrive together; energizes neighborhood commerce; and advances reuse. A proposed use of funds includes launching a small-scale pilot test in a single neighborhood or town to validate user adoption and gather feedback before a wider launch. The team also cites efforts to build an audience via community connections and targeted marketing.

## Risks & Challenges

-   **App development & dependencies:** Feature additions, testing needs, or changes by third-party mapping/payment services could cause delays. Mitigation: use an experienced development team, set clear milestones, and provide regular updates.
-   **Physical reward fulfillment:** Merchandise depends on printing/production/shipping schedules. Mitigation: reliable suppliers already sourced; timelines to be confirmed before fulfillment; prompt communication and timeline adjustments if needed.
-   **Audience growth:** Adoption depends on attracting both shoppers and sellers. Mitigation: active social outreach, local-business partnerships, and planned marketing campaigns. The proposed pilot test is intended to specifically address this challenge by testing adoption mechanics in a controlled environment. The creators commit to transparent communication, regular progress reports, and keeping supporters informed throughout.

## Team & Partnerships

The project is led by the founders, drawing on an experienced development team for build/testing. The page mentions relationships with reliable merchandise suppliers and outreach to local businesses; no specific organizations or individuals are named.

## Support & Post-Launch Plans

The team promises regular updates and open communication about progress and any changes to delivery expectations. Post-crowdfunding plans include a proposed, focused pilot launch to refine the app based on real-world use before expanding.

## One-Sentence Summary

A mobile app that aggregates local yard, estate, and community sales on a single live map, plans efficient routes, and adds game-like rewards to turn bargain hunting into a community-strengthening adventure.

## Problem

The creators describe weekend "treasure hunts" devolving into frustrating scavenger work: listings are scattered across social groups, random sites, fading street signs, and half-remembered addresses, causing wasted time, fuel, and missed finds. There's no comprehensive, real-time map for all types of sales, making planning difficult and inefficient.

## Solution / Product Overview

The product centralizes every kind of local sale---yard, estate, flea, vendor markets, church bazaars, and pop-ups---onto one interactive map. It helps users discover events any day of the week, plot an organized route, and enjoy a "modern treasure hunt" that also channels foot traffic to nearby small businesses.

## Key Features & Capabilities

-   Unified discovery of multiple sale types (yard, estate, flea, vendor fairs, church bazaars, neighborhood pop-ups).
-   Route planning to streamline multi-stop outings.
-   Gamification: surprise "Treasure Drops," collectible "doubloons," community leaderboards, and an in-app redemption area ("Plunder Pantry") for real-world merchandise.
-   Local-business support: optional geo-fenced ads that surface modest, location-triggered offers from nearby shops.
-   Emphasis on reuse/upcycling by keeping quality goods in circulation and out of landfills.

## Target Users & Use Cases

Designed for families, casual shoppers, and serious resellers seeking efficient discovery of local sales; for community explorers who want an engaging weekend activity; and for nearby small businesses aiming to reach shoppers traveling between sale stops.

## Why Crowdfunding / Use of Funds

Support is framed as enabling development of a single-map hub that helps shoppers, sellers, and local businesses thrive together; energizes neighborhood commerce; and advances reuse. A proposed use of funds includes launching a small-scale pilot test in a single neighborhood or town to validate user adoption and gather feedback before a wider launch. The proposed pilot would aim for a specific, small-scale metric, such as a goal of attracting 100 active users and 20 listing sellers during the pilot phase. The team also cites efforts to build an audience via community connections and targeted marketing.

## Risks & Challenges

-   **App development & dependencies:** Feature additions, testing needs, or changes by third-party mapping/payment services could cause delays. Mitigation: use an experienced development team, set clear milestones, and provide regular updates.
-   **Physical reward fulfillment:** Merchandise depends on printing/production/shipping schedules. Mitigation: reliable suppliers already sourced; timelines to be confirmed before fulfillment; prompt communication and timeline adjustments if needed.
-   **Audience growth:** Adoption depends on attracting both shoppers and sellers. Mitigation: active social outreach, local-business partnerships, and planned marketing campaigns. The proposed pilot test is intended to specifically address this challenge by testing adoption mechanics in a controlled environment. The creators commit to transparent communication, regular progress reports, and keeping supporters informed throughout.

## Team & Partnerships

The project is led by the founders, drawing on an experienced development team for build/testing. The page mentions relationships with reliable merchandise suppliers and outreach to local businesses; no specific organizations or individuals are named.

## Support & Post-Launch Plans

The team promises regular updates and open communication about progress and any changes to delivery expectations. Post-crowdfunding plans include a proposed, focused pilot launch to refine the app based on real-world use before expanding.

## One-Sentence Summary

A mobile app that aggregates local yard, estate, and community sales on a single live map, plans efficient routes, and adds game-like rewards to turn bargain hunting into a community-strengthening adventure.

## Problem

The creators describe weekend "treasure hunts" devolving into frustrating scavenger work: listings are scattered across social groups, random sites, fading street signs, and half-remembered addresses, causing wasted time, fuel, and missed finds. There's no comprehensive, real-time map for all types of sales, making planning difficult and inefficient.

## Solution / Product Overview

The product centralizes every kind of local sale---yard, estate, flea, vendor markets, church bazaars, and pop-ups---onto one interactive map. It helps users discover events any day of the week, plot an organized route, and enjoy a "modern treasure hunt" that also channels foot traffic to nearby small businesses.

## Key Features & Capabilities

-   Unified discovery of multiple sale types (yard, estate, flea, vendor fairs, church bazaars, neighborhood pop-ups).
-   Route planning to streamline multi-stop outings.
-   Gamification: surprise "Treasure Drops," collectible "doubloons," community leaderboards, and an in-app redemption area ("Plunder Pantry") for real-world merchandise.
-   Local-business support: optional geo-fenced ads that surface modest, location-triggered offers from nearby shops.
-   Emphasis on reuse/upcycling by keeping quality goods in circulation and out of landfills.

## Target Users & Use Cases

Designed for families, casual shoppers, and serious resellers seeking efficient discovery of local sales; for community explorers who want an engaging weekend activity; and for nearby small businesses aiming to reach shoppers traveling between sale stops.

## Why Crowdfunding / Use of Funds

Support is framed as enabling development of a single-map hub that helps shoppers, sellers, and local businesses thrive together; energizes neighborhood commerce; and advances reuse. A proposed use of funds includes launching a small-scale pilot test in a single neighborhood or town to validate user adoption and gather feedback before a wider launch. The proposed pilot would aim for a specific, small-scale metric, such as a goal of attracting 100 active users and 20 listing sellers during the pilot phase. The team also cites efforts to build an audience via community connections and targeted marketing. Additionally, a portion of funds is proposed to support a focused pre-pilot test of the "Treasure Drops" gamification mechanic with a small, defined user group (e.g., 20 beta testers) to validate engagement and refine the feature before the broader pilot launch.

## Risks & Challenges

-   **App development & dependencies:** Feature additions, testing needs, or changes by third-party mapping/payment services could cause delays. Mitigation: use an experienced development team, set clear milestones, and provide regular updates.
-   **Physical reward fulfillment:** Merchandise depends on printing/production/shipping schedules. Mitigation: reliable suppliers already sourced; timelines to be confirmed before fulfillment; prompt communication and timeline adjustments if needed.
-   **Audience growth:** Adoption depends on attracting both shoppers and sellers. Mitigation: active social outreach, local-business partnerships, and planned marketing campaigns. The proposed pilot test and the proposed pre-pilot gamification test are intended to specifically address this challenge by testing adoption and engagement mechanics in controlled environments. The creators commit to transparent communication, regular progress reports, and keeping supporters informed throughout.

## Team & Partnerships

The project is led by the founders, drawing on an experienced development team for build/testing. The page mentions relationships with reliable merchandise suppliers and outreach to local businesses; no specific organizations or individuals are named.

## Support & Post-Launch Plans

The team promises regular updates and open communication about progress and any changes to delivery expectations. Post-crowdfunding plans include a proposed, focused pilot launch to refine the app based on real-world use before expanding. This plan now includes the proposed pre-pilot test of the "Treasure Drops" gamification mechanic to inform its final design.

The creators describe weekend "treasure hunts" devolving into frustrating scavenger work: listings are scattered across social groups, random sites, fading street signs, and half-remembered addresses, causing wasted time, fuel, and missed finds. - Route planning to streamline multi-stop outings.
- Gamification: surprise "Treasure Drops," collectible "doubloons," community leaderboards, and an in-app redemption area ("Plunder Pantry") for real-world merchandise.
- Local-business support: optional geo-fenced ads that surface modest, location-triggered offers from nearby shops.
- Emphasis on reuse/upcycling by keeping quality goods in circulation and out of landfills.

## Target Users & Use Cases

Designed for families, casual shoppers, and serious resellers seeking efficient discovery of local sales; for community explorers who want an engaging weekend activity; and for nearby small businesses aiming to reach shoppers traveling between sale stops.

Support is framed as enabling development of a single-map hub that helps shoppers, sellers, and local businesses thrive together; energizes neighborhood commerce; and advances reuse. A proposed use of funds includes launching a small-scale pilot test in a single neighborhood or town to validate user adoption and gather feedback before a wider launch. ## One-Sentence Summary

A mobile app that aggregates local yard, estate, and community sales on a single live map, plans efficient routes, and adds game-like rewards to turn bargain hunting into a community-strengthening adventure.

## Problem

The creators describe weekend "treasure hunts" devolving into frustrating scavenger work: listings are scattered across social groups, random sites, fading street signs, and half-remembered addresses, causing wasted time, fuel, and missed finds. There's no comprehensive, real-time map for all types of sales, making planning difficult and inefficient.

## Solution / Product Overview

The product centralizes every kind of local sale---yard, estate, flea, vendor markets, church bazaars, and pop-ups---onto one interactive map. It helps users discover events any day of the week, plot an organized route, and enjoy a "modern treasure hunt" that also channels foot traffic to nearby small businesses.

## Key Features & Capabilities

- Unified discovery of multiple sale types (yard, estate, flea, vendor fairs, church bazaars, neighborhood pop-ups).
- Route planning to streamline multi-stop outings.
- Gamification: surprise "Treasure Drops," collectible "doubloons," community leaderboards, and an in-app redemption area ("Plunder Pantry") for real-world merchandise.
- Local-business support: optional geo-fenced ads that surface modest, location-triggered offers from nearby shops.
- Emphasis on reuse/upcycling by keeping quality goods in circulation and out of landfills.

## Target Users & Use Cases

Designed for families, casual shoppers, and serious resellers seeking efficient discovery of local sales; for community explorers who want an engaging weekend activity; and for nearby small businesses aiming to reach shoppers traveling between sale stops.

## Why Crowdfunding / Use of Funds

Support is framed as enabling development of a single-map hub that helps shoppers, sellers, and local businesses thrive together; energizes neighborhood commerce; and advances reuse. A proposed use of funds includes launching a small-scale pilot test in a single neighborhood or town to validate user adoption and gather feedback before a wider launch. The proposed pilot would aim for a specific, small-scale metric, such as a goal of attracting 100 active users and 20 listing sellers during the pilot phase. The team also cites efforts to build an audience via community connections and targeted marketing. Additionally, a portion of funds is proposed to support a focused pre-pilot test of the "Treasure Drops" gamification mechanic with a small, defined user group (e.g., 20 beta testers) to validate engagement and refine the feature before the broader pilot launch. As part of this pilot strategy, the team proposes seeking a targeted partnership with a single, named local business association or community group in the pilot neighborhood to help source initial sale listings and add credibility to the community-strengthening claim. The team proposes targeting the **Maplewood Neighborhood Association** for this partnership.

## Risks & Challenges

## One-Sentence Summary

A mobile app that aggregates local yard, estate, and community sales on a single live map, plans efficient routes, and adds game-like rewards to turn bargain hunting into a community-strengthening adventure.

## Problem

The creators describe weekend "treasure hunts" devolving into frustrating scavenger work: listings are scattered across social groups, random sites, fading street signs, and half-remembered addresses, causing wasted time, fuel, and missed finds. There's no comprehensive, real-time map for all types of sales, making planning difficult and inefficient.

## Solution / Product Overview

The product centralizes every kind of local sale---yard, estate, flea, vendor markets, church bazaars, and pop-ups---onto one interactive map. It helps users discover events any day of the week, plot an organized route, and enjoy a "modern treasure hunt" that also channels foot traffic to nearby small businesses.

## Key Features & Capabilities

- Unified discovery of multiple sale types (yard, estate, flea, vendor fairs, church bazaars, neighborhood pop-ups).
- Route planning to streamline multi-stop outings.
- Gamification: surprise "Treasure Drops," collectible "doubloons," community leaderboards, and an in-app redemption area ("Plunder Pantry") for real-world merchandise.
- Local-business support: optional geo-fenced ads that surface modest, location-triggered offers from nearby shops.
- Emphasis on reuse/upcycling by keeping quality goods in circulation and out of landfills.

## Target Users & Use Cases

Designed for families, casual shoppers, and serious resellers seeking efficient discovery of local sales; for community explorers who want an engaging weekend activity; and for nearby small businesses aiming to reach shoppers traveling between sale stops.

## Why Crowdfunding / Use of Funds

Support is framed as enabling development of a single-map hub that helps shoppers, sellers, and local businesses thrive together; energizes neighborhood commerce; and advances reuse. A proposed use of funds includes launching a small-scale pilot test in a single neighborhood or town to validate user adoption and gather feedback before a wider launch. The proposed pilot would aim for a specific, small-scale metric, such as a goal of attracting 100 active users and 20 listing sellers during the pilot phase. The team also cites efforts to build an audience via community connections and targeted marketing. Additionally, a portion of funds is proposed to support a focused pre-pilot test of the "Treasure Drops" gamification mechanic with a small, defined user group (e.g., 20 beta testers) to validate engagement and refine the feature before the broader pilot launch. As part of this pilot strategy, the team proposes seeking a targeted partnership with a single, named local business association or community group in the pilot neighborhood to help source initial sale listings and add credibility to the community-strengthening claim. The team proposes targeting the **Maplewood Neighborhood Association** for this partnership. Furthermore, the team proposes a small, defined test of the local-business ad feature during the pilot, such as offering geo-fenced offers from 3-5 specific businesses in the Maplewood neighborhood to validate the concept.

## Risks & Challenges

- **App development & dependencies:** Feature additions, testing needs, or changes by third-party mapping/payment services could cause delays. Mitigation: use an experienced development team, set clear milestones, and provide regular updates.
- **Physical reward fulfillment:** Merchandise depends on printing/production/shipping schedules. Mitigation: reliable suppliers already sourced; timelines to be confirmed before fulfillment; prompt communication and timeline adjustments if needed.
- **Audience growth:** Adoption depends on attracting both shoppers and sellers. Mitigation: active social outreach, local-business partnerships, and planned marketing campaigns. The proposed pilot test, the proposed pre-pilot gamification test, the proposed targeted partnership with the Maplewood Neighborhood Association, and the proposed test of the local-business ad feature are intended to specifically address this challenge by testing adoption and engagement mechanics in controlled environments. The creators commit to transparent communication, regular progress reports, and keeping supporters informed throughout.

## Team & Partnerships

The project is led by the founders, drawing on an experienced development team for build/testing. The page mentions relationships with reliable merchandise suppliers and outreach to local businesses; no specific organizations or individuals are named. The team proposes seeking a partnership with the **Maplewood Neighborhood Association** as part of the pilot launch strategy.

## Support & Post-Launch Plans

The team promises regular updates and open communication about progress and any changes to delivery expectations. Post-crowdfunding plans include a proposed, focused pilot launch to refine the app based on real-world use before expanding. This plan now includes the proposed pre-pilot test of the "Treasure Drops" gamification mechanic to inform its final design, the proposed targeted partnership with the Maplewood Neighborhood Association to support initial listing acquisition and community credibility, and the proposed test of the local-business ad feature to validate its concept.

## One-Sentence Summary

A mobile app that aggregates local yard, estate, and community sales on a single live map, plans efficient routes, and adds game-like rewards to turn bargain hunting into a community-strengthening adventure.

## Problem

The creators describe weekend "treasure hunts" devolving into frustrating scavenger work: listings are scattered across social groups, random sites, fading street signs, and half-remembered addresses, causing wasted time, fuel, and missed finds. There's no comprehensive, real-time map for all types of sales, making planning difficult and inefficient.

## Solution / Product Overview

The product centralizes every kind of local sale---yard, estate, flea, vendor markets, church bazaars, and pop-ups---onto one interactive map. It helps users discover events any day of the week, plot an organized route, and enjoy a "modern treasure hunt" that also channels foot traffic to nearby small businesses.

## Key Features & Capabilities

- Unified discovery of multiple sale types (yard, estate, flea, vendor fairs, church bazaars, neighborhood pop-ups).
- Route planning to streamline multi-stop outings.
- Gamification: surprise "Treasure Drops," collectible "doubloons," community leaderboards, and an in-app redemption area ("Plunder Pantry") for real-world merchandise.
- Local-business support: optional geo-fenced ads that surface modest, location-triggered offers from nearby shops.
- Emphasis on reuse/upcycling by keeping quality goods in circulation and out of landfills.

## Target Users & Use Cases

Designed for families, casual shoppers, and serious resellers seeking efficient discovery of local sales; for community explorers who want an engaging weekend activity; and for nearby small businesses aiming to reach shoppers traveling between sale stops.

## Why Crowdfunding / Use of Funds

Support is framed as enabling development of a single-map hub that helps shoppers, sellers, and local businesses thrive together; energizes neighborhood commerce; and advances reuse. A proposed use of funds includes launching a small-scale pilot test in a single neighborhood or town to validate user adoption and gather feedback before a wider launch. The proposed pilot would aim for a specific, small-scale metric, such as a goal of attracting 100 active users and 20 listing sellers during the pilot phase. The team also cites efforts to build an audience via community connections and targeted marketing. Additionally, a portion of funds is proposed to support a focused pre-pilot test of the "Treasure Drops" gamification mechanic with a small, defined user group (e.g., 20 beta testers) to validate engagement and refine the feature before the broader pilot launch. For this pre-pilot test, the team proposes a specific, small-scale metric, such as targeting 70% of the 20 beta testers to engage with at least one Treasure Drop. As part of this pilot strategy, the team proposes seeking a targeted partnership with a single, named local business association or community group in the pilot neighborhood to help source initial sale listings and add credibility to the community-strengthening claim. The team proposes targeting the **Maplewood Neighborhood Association** for this partnership. Furthermore, the team proposes a small, defined test of the local-business ad feature during the pilot, such as offering geo-fenced offers from 3-5 specific businesses in the Maplewood neighborhood to validate the concept.

## Risks & Challenges

- **App development & dependencies:** Feature additions, testing needs, or changes by third-party mapping/payment services could cause delays. Mitigation: use an experienced development team, set clear milestones, and provide regular updates.
- **Physical reward fulfillment:** Merchandise depends on printing/production/shipping schedules. Mitigation: reliable suppliers already sourced; timelines to be confirmed before fulfillment; prompt communication and timeline adjustments if needed.
- **Audience growth:** Adoption depends on attracting both shoppers and sellers. Mitigation: active social outreach, local-business partnerships, and planned marketing campaigns. The proposed pilot test, the proposed pre-pilot gamification test (including its proposed engagement metric), the proposed targeted partnership with the Maplewood Neighborhood Association, and the proposed test of the local-business ad feature are intended to specifically address this challenge by testing adoption and engagement mechanics in controlled environments. The creators commit to transparent communication, regular progress reports, and keeping supporters informed throughout.

A mobile app that aggregates local yard, estate, and community sales on a single live map, plans efficient routes, and adds game-like rewards to turn bargain hunting into a community-strengthening adventure.

## Problem

The creators describe weekend "treasure hunts" devolving into frustrating scavenger work: listings are scattered across social groups, random sites, fading street signs, and half-remembered addresses, causing wasted time, fuel, and missed finds. There's no comprehensive, real-time map for all types of sales, making planning difficult and inefficient.

## Solution / Product Overview

The product centralizes every kind of local sale---yard, estate, flea, vendor markets, church bazaars, and pop-ups---onto one interactive map. It helps users discover events any day of the week, plot an organized route, and enjoy a "modern treasure hunt" that also channels foot traffic to nearby small businesses.

- Unified discovery of multiple sale types (yard, estate, flea, vendor fairs, church bazaars, neighborhood pop-ups).
- Route planning to streamline multi-stop outings.
- Gamification: surprise "Treasure Drops," collectible "doubloons," community leaderboards, and an in-app redemption area ("Plunder Pantry") for real-world merchandise.
- Local-business support: optional geo-fenced ads that surface modest, location-triggered offers from nearby shops.
- Emphasis on reuse/upcycling by keeping quality goods in circulation and out of landfills.

The team also proposes a small, defined test of the route-planning feature's efficiency during the pilot, such as comparing the average distance traveled by 10 pilot users using the app's route planner versus a manually planned route for the same set of sales.
